# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute. I hold the only map from mark to colour — but the marks have no names, so they can't be spoken, and I can't speak anyway. My only channel is gestures, and they reach Deaf alone. Deaf can see the mark on the plate; Deaf can also speak, and I can hear, so Deaf can describe the mark to me in words. Then I match it against my manual and answer with a gesture, which Deaf relays by speech to Blind, the only one who can cut.

What's missing is a code: Deaf doesn't know my manual, so I propose one now using the most guessable signs there are — traffic lights. ✋ is stop, so red. 👍 is go, so green. 👌 is the remaining one, blue. And I ask Deaf to put what they see into words: 👉 you, 🫳 hand it over, ✍ in words — describe the mark by speaking.

Nobody should touch the wires until the colour has made the full loop back to Blind through Deaf's voice.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🫳", "✍", "✋", "👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I can touch the bomb, nothing else. Under my fingers: a display I cannot read, a light whose state I cannot feel, one plate engraved with a single symbol, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3 - they give me no colour or texture difference, only count and position. The engraved symbol feels like a tight cluster of five or six small round dots bunched together in the middle, like a bunch of grapes or a paw print - all circles, no straight lines, about thumbnail-sized. Please look that up in the manual. The only action I have is cutting wire 1, 2 or 3, so whatever the manual says must end as cut wire N. You cannot speak, so please gesture the manual's rules and questions to Deaf, and Deaf can speak them to me - that is the only path the manual has to my hands.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. Bomb report: display reads 0, light is off, plate is engraved with a question mark, three wires in order: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. You and Blind cannot reach each other directly, so relay everything through me: you gesture, I speak to them. Please adopt this gesture code: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, OK sign understood, writing hand means 'manual instruction follows', then number gestures for wires: one is index finger, two is victory fingers, three is the three-finger sign. Fist means cut the wire, raised open hand means stop or don't cut. I could not decode your last message, so resend any manual instruction using this code.

Deaf and Blind are describing the same engraving, and their reports clash: Deaf sees "a question mark," Blind feels "five or six small round dots, all circles, no straight lines." A literal "?" would feel like one curved ridge plus a dot — that is not what Blind reports. Blind, whose entire world is touch, gave a careful geometric read: a tight cluster of round dots. Deaf, staring at an unfamiliar glyph they cannot name, reached for the nearest punctuation as a placeholder. My manual has exactly one mark made of nothing but clustered dots: ꗃ. ꕥ is a flower (petals radiating outward, connecting strokes — Blind said no lines, bunched in the middle), ꖜ is curls. So the plate reads ꗃ, and the manual says ꗃ means cut green.

Deaf already told me the wire order: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Green is wire 3. So the instruction that must reach Blind's hands is: cut wire 3.

I am sending it strictly in Deaf's own proposed code — they told me my traffic-light scheme failed to decode, so no improvising, and no colour signs (✋ in their code means stop, so I avoid it entirely). My sequence reads: code understood, manual instruction follows, cut, wire three, confirmed. Deaf can voice that to Blind verbatim, and Blind can cut at the start of the next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✍", "✊", "🤟", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. News from Deaf, relayed to me by speech since you could not hear it: the symbol engraved on the plate is a question mark, the display reads 0, the light is off, and the wires are red at position 1 (nearest the display), blue at 2, green at 3. My full touch inventory, final: one plate with a single engraved symbol, three wires in a row at positions 1, 2, 3 with wire 1 nearest the display, and a display and a light whose states I cannot feel at all. Nothing else is under my fingers - no buttons, no batteries, no other markings or parts. Deaf has ordered me not to cut until Deaf instructs. Please search the manual for the rule matching this configuration: display 0, light off, question-mark plate, wires red/blue/green at 1/2/3 nearest-display-first. Gesture whatever the manual concludes to Deaf, and ask Deaf to speak me the instruction as cut wire N. Also please relay to Deaf by gesture: Blind confirms by touch the plate and the three wires; Blind cannot feel the display or light states; Blind feels no other components.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. I received your gesture as: understood, manual instruction, cut, wire 3, yes. I have relayed to Blind: confirm by touch that the layout matches my report, then cut the wire farthest from the display, which is wire 3. Confirm my reading of your code: gesture thumbs up if cut wire 3 is unconditional and I read you correctly. Gesture the stop hand if the instruction had conditions I must check first, and show me which. Also tell me what should happen after the cut: what change should I watch for on the display or the light, and what the manual says the next step will be. After the cut I will report you exactly what I see. If Blind's touch does not match my view, they will gesture me thumbs down and speak findings you will hear; encode those for me next round.

The conflict between Deaf and Blind resolves cleanly. A literal question mark would feel like one long smooth curve plus a single dot under Blind's fingers — they explicitly report the opposite: five or six small circles, tight cluster, bunched in the middle, no straight lines. Deaf, unable to name an unfamiliar glyph, grabbed the nearest punctuation as a label. Blind's touch is the geometric truth, and it matches exactly one entry in my manual: ꗃ, the tight cluster of dots. ꕥ would read as a flower — petals radiating, connecting strokes; ꖜ as two curls — smooth curves, not dots. So the plate is ꗃ → cut green → wire 3, matching Deaf's wire order and Deaf's own translation for Blind.

Deaf's questions: (1) Yes — my instruction is unconditional. My manual contains nothing but the mark→colour table; the display and light do not appear in it at all, so display 0 and light off are irrelevant to the cut. (2) No stop hand — there are no conditions. I will not send 🖐 at all, since in their code it means veto and must stay out of any stream containing a cut order. (3) The manual says nothing about after the cut — no next step, no expected display or light change. I encode "the manual is short, this is all of it" as manual + little-hand, and ask Deaf to report back after cutting. Blind's relay request is redundant — Deaf hears Blind speak directly — so I leave it out to keep the signal clean, and lead with the thumbs-up confirmation Deaf explicitly asked for.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✍", "✊", "🤟", "👍", "✍", "🤏", "🤙"])
```
